No backend, contract or API change; no new source comments. adminRuntime.test.ts is 735 lines. tally reports overlaps with fx-admin-funds and fx-admin-values on http.ts, http.test.ts and both runtime test files.
--- Commits 1 to 3 (details in the earlier hand-offs and commit bodies) ---

1: a 5xx body that is not JSON becomes ApiError (INTERNAL_ERROR, reply status). Red 4f4b0e18, 82f42121, b00e0394, 743089d9. Checks on 812b174: 71e96d42, cd5b5d22 (44 files, 389 tests), 13f54d99 (17 assets, 954009 bytes), d8236e27.

2: a failed body read becomes TransportError offline; a caller cancel is left alone. Red 986cf4f4, 9a8fb95b, 547a2ebc, 1194b348; void run 20d97f4c. Checks on 2909bbb: 1b364b1e, e956481b (44 files, 393 tests), 9d4f97fe (17 assets, 954174 bytes), 3ad53148.

3: all four refresh executors rethrow an outage instead of ending the session. Red 3b1183b4, e3e876ac, 8502ead1. Checks on 223718f (F4: the body lacked these): contracts ad06f9b3; check 8d0121ad, 44 files, 396 tests; build:client 8bc03f00, 17 assets, 954214 bytes, boot 7 chunks; build:admin 2da44e1d, boot 7 chunks.
Correction to 1's body (review 1 F3): a failing query now sends up to 9 requests (React Query retries included), not 'retries twice'.

Correction to 3's body and hand-off (review 2 F4): 'a native restore meeting such an outage rejects, showing the retry splash' holds only when no access token is stored, so the restore refreshes first. The usual APK case is a stored access token that has expired. There the session read's refresh meets the outage, nativeRestore's catch returns null and the sign-in screen shows. That part is older than this lane. Since 223718f the tokens and held writes are kept there; before, the failed refresh ended the session and cleared them.
--- Commit 4 (second lane review) ---

F1 (MEDIUM, from 223718f): the outage a failed refresh rethrew was retryable. The transport loop re-ran the read and its refresh (whose CSRF read retries 3 times itself), and React Query re-ran the query. Up to 36 requests per read, or about 9 minutes of loading when the CSRF read hangs.

F1 fix: sendWithAuthRecovery rethrows a refresh failure through withoutRetry, a non-retryable copy of the same ApiError or TransportError (kind, status, code and message kept). TransportError gains a readonly retryable flag (default: kind is not malformed, the old behaviour), and both isRetryable (React Query's policy in QueryProvider) and the transport's isRetryableFailure now read it. Such a read now sends its GET once plus the refresh's own attempts (3 CSRF tries for a retryable outage), then shows its outage error. isOutage, isUnknownWriteOutcome and the error variants are unchanged, so writes stay sent once, unknown, same key on Check again. ClientFailure.retryable is not read by any UI, and AsyncBoundary always offers Try again.

F2 (LOW): the refresh executors and both cookie restores now keep the session on isTemporaryFailure, meaning an outage or any ApiError with status 429. The admin helper is renamed clearUnlessOutage -> clearUnlessTemporary. Every other non-outage failure still ends the session as before: 401, 403, malformed, a 2xx that fails the contract, and 'replaced'.

F2 needs nginx's HTML 429 recognised. readBody now reads a non-JSON 429 as no body, and failFromResponse builds ApiError RATE_LIMITED (status 429, not retryable, message 'Too many requests just now. Wait a moment and try again.'). Other non-JSON 4xx stay malformed. Side effect, disclosed: a write meeting nginx's 429 page directly now reads like the backend's JSON 429. A first submit says Nothing changed (nginx limit_req/limit_conn refuse before proxying, so nothing applied); Check again stays unknown (isUnknownRetryOutcome lists RATE_LIMITED). Before, it was malformed, which is unknown.

F2 side effect, disclosed: a direct 429 on the restore's own CSRF recovery or session read now keeps the store too. The screen shows signed out (SessionProvider counts only isOutage as restoring), with the principal and holds kept. This is the same accepted residue as a CSRF outage at reload (finding-57).

Tests 4 (8 new cases): http 'fails a read once with $way: one send and one refresh, retried neither by the transport nor by the query' for a lost connection and a 502 ApiError. It counts fetch and refresh calls, checks no sleep, and runs createQueryClient's own retry policy on the error. Admin restore table: 'has its session read's refresh meet a proxy's 502 page' and '... nginx's 429 page' both keep the admin and 2 held writes. Admin 'keeps the admin and the held writes, and Check again unknown, when the browser's CSRF recovery meets $way' for nginx's 429 page and a JSON RATE_LIMITED. Admin APK 'ends the admin APK's session and clears the held writes when the refresh is refused with 401'. Client 'ends the tab's session when the CSRF recovery refuses the refresh with 401'.

Red 4 (each from the saved .c4 copy, restored and cmp'd; all failed only their targets): F1 rethrow removed ae6c7cbb-77c0-4cd2-9479-9e91c11e962f 2 of 31; executors back to outage-only 37ba6432-a9b5-4f8a-a2fd-4c4d744f7a0e 3 of 35; nginx 429 no longer mapped efbb470d-f23b-4686-8e55-4c2e834b2760 2 of 35; restore clear back to outage-only a79598c0-1fe2-4de6-b503-9c97376e65a9 1 of 35; executors back to catch-all (restore 502 row) ae6eaa1d-f021-477c-b58a-adeda748aa6f 6 of 35; APK native executor rethrows everything 9d7e05ec-16fc-474b-b8ed-542e427235f0 1 of 35; client cookie executor rethrows everything 2c575256-491d-44df-8826-1ff99c54effa 1 of 18.

Checks 4 on a61f76f, clean tree, Node 24 container: contracts npm ci && npm run build 8ae86866-1227-4328-b7df-f2dbbe5fad4b green; frontend npm ci && npm run check 2391ef76-3a12-4b99-94b0-9dd48dfd2af5 green, 44 files, 404 tests (typecheck, lint, generate:api:check, build, boot 7 chunks, phonepe target check); build:client 45d1d2b3-e7d3-44a6-b26c-24067f61ddf4 green, 17 assets, 954688 bytes, boot 7 chunks; build:admin 0eac5dee-900e-44d7-b7cf-b0aa08680c52 green, boot 7 chunks.

Not covered by a test: the client APK refresh (same line as the others). Open from review 2 section 3: whether every refresh refusal is a 401 or 403 (webAuth.ts executeTakeFirstOrThrow would answer 500 for a missing user row, which now keeps the tab), and whether a lost cookie refresh gets the 30-second rotationId grace.
Evidence label: TESTED for all four commits. Behind a real proxy: UNVERIFIED.
--- Runtime steps for the coordinator ---

Step A (1, admin web): with a hold showing Not confirmed, stop the backend behind the proxy so /v1/auth/web/csrf and /v1/admin/session answer nginx's 502 page, then reload (signed out or restoring is expected). Bring the backend back and reload: the same admin restores, the hold and Not confirmed are still there, and Check again settles with the same Idempotency-Key. Client: same with /v1/auth/client/web/csrf.
Step B (2): as A, with the proxy cutting the CSRF reply mid-body. First confirm that with proxy_buffering off response.text() really rejects.

Step C (3, admin web): with a hold showing Not confirmed, delete the admin access cookie (keep the refresh cookie) and block */v1/auth/web/csrf (a DevTools block gives a lost connection; a proxy 502 on that path gives a 502). Press Check again: still signed in, no session-ended notice, the hold stays. Unblock and press Check again: it refreshes and settles with the same key.

Step D (4): same setup as C. Open a list screen, a read. The Network panel should show the read once, then the CSRF tries (3 for a 502/503/timeout, 1 for a DevTools block), then nothing more. The error shows within about 2 s for fast failures, or about 61 s if the CSRF read hangs; before, up to 36 requests. Then make /v1/auth/web/csrf answer 429 (a proxy rule, or exceed the general zone) and press Check again on a hold: the tab stays signed in and the hold stays Not confirmed.

Commit 812b17430e063386324171ee71579c34a6e2bba1 on track/fx-outage-502 (parent 3ce9be9): fix(api): count a 5xx reply that is not JSON as an outage. Author/committer tamagami-hi, no trailers. Not pushed, not landed.

Files: frontend_stack_ts/src/api/http.ts (+1 line), src/api/http.test.ts, src/shells/admin/adminRuntime.test.ts, src/shells/client/clientRuntime.test.ts. No runtime source change in the shells; no backend, contract or API change; no new source comments.

Defect (C3): readBody threw TransportError malformed for any non-JSON body, so a proxy 502 HTML page was not isOutage; both cookie restores cleared the session and the admin clear dropped every held write.

Fix: in readBody, a body that fails JSON.parse with status >= 500 is read as null, like an empty 5xx already was. The reply then goes through the maintenance check and failFromResponse: ApiError INTERNAL_ERROR, status = reply status, retryable true. isOutage, isUnknownWriteOutcome and the maintenance check now agree.
Unchanged: 2xx non-JSON stays TransportError malformed (existing test 'reports a body that is not JSON as malformed'); 4xx non-JSON stays malformed.

Write outcome, checked before changing anything: there is no src/api/writeOutcome.ts; the classifier is isUnknownWriteOutcome/isUnknownRetryOutcome in src/api/errors.ts (tested by src/api/writeOutcome.test.ts). A non-ApiError, malformed included, was already unknown, and an ApiError with status >= 500 is unknown, so a keyed write stays Not confirmed with Check again both before and after the fix.
Behaviour change to note: a GET that meets a proxy 5xx page now retries on the 300/900 ms ladder like any retryable 5xx (malformed was not retried). Writes are never retried (one send per request).

Tests (5 new cases, no new files): http 'counts a proxy's 502 page ... as an outage' and 'keeps a keyed write that meets a proxy's 502 page unknown ... same key'; admin restore table +2 rows (502 page on CSRF recovery keeps stored admin + 2 held writes; on session read rejects, keeps admin + 2 held writes); client 'keeps the stored principal ... proxy's 502 page'.

Client note: the client app keeps no held writes in storage (only the admin heldWriteStore/heldRecordings use sessionStorage), so the client case asserts the principal and its stored localStorage copy are kept.

Red controls (fix reverted in isolation, then restored and cmp'd against .temp/fx-outage-502/http.ts.fixed): http 4f4b0e18-851d-49c5-b2ad-3959254ae4ec failed 1 of 26 (the outage case; the keyed-write case passed there); admin 82f42121-2dbd-4e28-90dc-e9c2988361c7 failed 2 of 27; client b00e0394-bae8-4b85-bad9-0228d648ff05 failed 1 of 16.

Keyed-write control: with the fix kept, isUnknownWriteOutcome was mutated so a 5xx counts as nothing applied: 743089d9-f7af-426a-974e-ed8c81482d6e failed 1 of 26 (only that case). errors.ts restored from the saved copy (cmp equal, git diff empty). Note: after the usage pause, errors.ts still held this mutation, not the fix; it was run and restored before the commit, which does not touch errors.ts.

Expect: still signed in as the same admin, the hold and Not confirmed still there, Check again sends the same Idempotency-Key and settles it.

Runtime step (client web): signed in, stop the backend behind the proxy so /v1/auth/client/web/csrf answers a 502 HTML page, reload, bring the backend back, reload: the client restores as the same user without signing in again; nothing is cleared at the outage reload.

Sibling not fixed (rule 15, recorded for the coordinator): if response.text() itself rejects without the deadline (connection reset mid-body), sendOnce rethrows the raw cause (a TypeError), which isOutage does not count, so a restore would still clear the session and admin holds. --- Commit 2 (same class: body breaks off mid-read) ---

Defect: when response.text() rejected without the deadline (connection reset partway through the reply), sendOnce rethrew the raw cause (a TypeError); isOutage ignores it, so a restore cleared the session and the admin's held writes.

Fix: in the body-read catch, after the deadline check: a TransportError (the malformed parse) is reported and rethrown as before; a cancel by the caller (options.signal aborted) is rethrown unchanged, not reported and not retried (it used to be reported as malformed; now matches the fetch path); anything else is reported offline and thrown as TransportError offline. isOutage, the GET retry ladder and the write outcome treat it like any lost connection.

Tests 2 (4 new cases): http 'counts a body that breaks off mid-read ... as a lost connection and an outage' (real Response over a ReadableStream that errors with TypeError after a partial chunk); 'leaves a cancel by the caller during the body read as the caller's own cancel, sent once'; the keyed-write test became a table with a 'body that breaks off mid-read' row (201, same key on Check again); admin restore row 'meets a body that breaks off on the CSRF recovery' keeps the stored admin and 2 held writes. No client case: no stored holds there.

--- Commit 3 (review F1, older than the lane) ---

Defect: all four refresh executors (admin and client, cookie and native) caught every failure as 'unauthenticated', so http.ts sendWithAuthRecovery ended the session as expired and the admin clear wiped every held write, even when the refresh met a timeout, lost connection, proxy 502 page, broken-off body or JSON 5xx.

Fix: each executor's catch now rethrows an error that isOutage accepts and returns 'unauthenticated' otherwise. http.ts needs no change: a rejected refreshOnce already propagates out of the 401 branch before endSession, so the original request fails with the refresh's own outage error. Nothing is ended or cleared; the refresh's failed request has already reported its outcome through the runtime's bare client, so the network banner shows it.

Why no 'unreachable' outcome: a string outcome cannot carry the outage error. Throwing the original 401 instead would leave a failed read blank (AsyncBoundary returns null for isSessionEnded errors) and turn a first submit into Nothing changed. Throwing a made-up generic error would lose the real cause.

Still ends the session: a 401 or 403 from the refresh (any non-outage failure: CSRF_INVALID, RATE_LIMITED, malformed), and the refresh-finds-another-user case (replaced, finding-50/a1789ef). Both unchanged.

Native: the native executors share this path (http.ts -> refreshCoordinator), so they are covered. Side effect: a native restore whose access token is missing and whose refresh meets an outage now rejects with that outage (SessionProvider 'restoring' with an error, so the splash offers retry), where it used to resolve signed out. Native restores never cleared tokens either way. The admin cookie restore's session read gets the same benefit: a refresh outage there now keeps the store instead of clearing it.

Residual (not changed): if the refresh POST itself is lost after the server rotated, the next refresh may be refused as reuse and end the session then, clearing holds under the existing session-end rule.
